title: Dhaka ranked world's most polluted major city, AQI above 250
detail: IQAir reported Dhaka's AQI above 250 (hazardous range) on 14 January, ranking it the most polluted major city, citing brick kilns, traffic and construction dust amid stagnant winter air.

title: HRSS: 10 killed, 2,503 hurt over election period; polling day largely peaceful
detail: Human Rights Support Society counted over 700 election-related violence incidents from October 2025 to 14 February 2026, with 10 dead and 2,503 injured; its observers logged 393 polling-day irregularities including 105 supporter clashes but no polling-day deaths.

title: HRSS: 10 killed, 1,933 hurt in election-month violence
detail: Human Rights Support Society recorded 346 political violence incidents in February 2026, the month of the 13th parliamentary election, leaving 10 dead and 1,933 injured; most involved BNP-Jamaat clashes and intra-BNP feuds.

title: Train hits bus at Cumilla level crossing, 12 dead
detail: A Dhaka-bound train struck a bus that had entered the tracks at the Padua Bazar level crossing on the Dhaka-Chattogram highway, killing 12; rail traffic was suspended for about three hours and two gatemen were suspended.
attribution: Police and fire service via AIR

title: 13 fishermen seized on Naf River, allegedly by Arakan Army
detail: Thirteen Bangladeshi fishermen from Shah Porir Dwip were seized on the Naf River by armed men on speedboats, allegedly Arakan Army, and taken into Myanmar; BGB data cited says at least 399 fishermen have been taken since Dec 2024.
attribution: Daily Star commentary citing BGB data via New Age

title: Gas lighter factory fire kills 5 in Keraniganj
detail: A fire at a gas lighter factory in the Kadamtali area of Keraniganj killed at least five people; seven fire service units took several hours to control it and the cause was under investigation.
attribution: Fire Service and Civil Defence via AP

title: ~250 missing after Teknaf trawler sinks in Andaman Sea
detail: UNHCR and IOM said about 250 Rohingya and Bangladeshis were missing after an overcrowded trawler that left Teknaf for Malaysia sank in rough seas; nine were rescued on 9 April, six of whom were detained as alleged traffickers.
attribution: UNHCR and IOM joint statement via Al Jazeera

title: Load-shedding exceeds 2,000 MW; 15+ plants offline
detail: Power Grid Bangladesh figures showed supply of 13,198 MW against 15,200 MW demand, with over 15 plants shut by fuel shortages linked to Middle East disruption of LNG imports and faults; rural areas faced 8-10 hour outages during the heatwave.
attribution: Power Grid Bangladesh data via TBS

title: WHO: measles in 58 of 64 districts, 166 deaths
detail: WHO reported 19,161 suspected and 2,897 confirmed measles cases with 166 deaths between 15 March and 14 April 2026, across all eight divisions (Dhaka 8,263 cases); a nationwide measles-rubella campaign for children 6-59 months began 20 April and WHO rated national risk high.
attribution: World Health Organization, citing national surveillance

title: Mild-to-moderate heatwave; Jashore peaks at 38°C
detail: BMD said a mild-to-moderate heatwave covered Khulna division, Dhaka, Rajshahi and other districts, with a high of 38°C in Jashore, and could begin to ease with rain; power supply ran about 200 MW short at peak.

title: Two Bangladeshis killed by BSF pellet fire, Kasba
detail: BGB said two Bangladeshi men, part of a group of about 15 alleged smugglers who crossed into India, died in an Indian hospital after a BSF member fired pellets during a scuffle near the Dhajanagar-Pathariyadwar border late on 8 May.
attribution: BGB account via The Daily Star

title: Measles deaths among children pass 500
detail: Al Jazeera reported the health department tally at 512 child deaths from measles since 15 March 2026, with Dhaka hospitals overwhelmed; the outbreak is described as the deadliest in decades.
attribution: Bangladesh health department tally via Al Jazeera

title: UNHCR: 152,029 new Rohingya arrivals since Dec 2024
detail: UNHCR said 152,029 newly arrived Rohingya were registered between December 2024 and 31 May 2026, including 2,260 in May 2026, fleeing violence in Rakhine State; about 1.2 million Rohingya are in the camps.

title: M4.5 quake near Silchar felt in Dhaka and Sylhet
detail: BMD said a magnitude 4.5 earthquake at 10 km depth near Silchar, Assam, about 92 km east of Sylhet, was felt in Dhaka and elsewhere at about 21:40; no damage was reported.
place: Near Silchar (Assam), ~92 km E of Sylhet

title: Bangladeshi killed in BSF firing, Kulaura border
detail: A Bangladeshi villager was killed in BSF firing near border pillars 1852-1853 (Nishchintapur/Dattagram area); BGB 46 Battalion said BSF took the body to an Indian hospital morgue and would hand it over after legal procedures.
attribution: BGB 46 Battalion, local police via TBS

title: BGB blocks BSF push-in of 20 people, Shibganj
detail: BGB's Mahananda 59 Battalion said Chouka border outpost members prevented BSF from pushing 20 people into Bangladesh; the group remained on the Indian side at the zero line.

title: Quake centred at Rupganj jolts Dhaka
detail: An earthquake centred at Rupganj, Narayanganj, about 16 km northeast of Dhaka at 16 km depth struck at about 21:28; USGS put it at M4.4 and BMD at 4.0, with no immediate reports of casualties.

title: BFIU froze ~55,000 MFS accounts over gambling and hundi
detail: Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury told parliament the BFIU had suspended about 55,000 mobile financial service accounts suspected of online gambling and digital hundi; Bangladesh Bank issued MFS monitoring directives on 28 May.

title: RSF: 438 killed in 472 road crashes in June
detail: Road Safety Foundation counted 472 road crashes in June 2026 killing 438 and injuring 561; motorcycles accounted for 134 deaths and pedestrians 91.

title: Rights group: 10 Bangladeshis killed by BSF in H1 2026
detail: Ain o Salish Kendra said, based on newspaper reports, that 10 Bangladeshis were killed in BSF border violence in January-June 2026 (7 shot, 3 after torture), with 10 injured and 1 abducted across 21 incidents.
attribution: Ain o Salish Kendra (ASK), compiled from media reports

title: Chattogram records 412 mm in 24 hours, highest in 43 years
detail: BMD recorded 412 mm of rain in Chattogram in the 24 hours to 15:00 Tuesday, the highest 24-hour total in 43 years, from a Bay of Bengal low-pressure system; a further 179.4 mm fell over the next 24 hours.

title: Landslides kill 22 in Chattogram region over three days
detail: Landslides and wall collapses after record rain killed 22 people over three days in Cox's Bazar, Chattogram and Rangamati, including five madrasa students in Ukhiya when a retaining wall collapsed.

title: Landslides kill at least 18 Rohingya, mostly children
detail: At least 18 Rohingya, mostly children, were killed in landslides and a wall collapse at a madrasa in the Ukhiya and Teknaf camps; officials said more than 200 landslides and flash floods had destroyed thousands of shelters.
attribution: Refugee Relief and Repatriation Commission (RRRC) official via Arab News

title: FFWC: 10 districts at flood risk; Sangu 190 cm over danger
detail: FFWC warned of flooding in 24-72 hours in Feni, Chattogram, Khagrachhari, Sylhet, Netrokona, Sherpur, Mymensingh, Lalmonirhat, Kurigram and Gaibandha; the Sangu at Bandarban was 190 cm above danger level and the Matamuhuri at Lama 18 cm above.

title: FFWC: Surma-Kushiyara rising, Sylhet floods may worsen
detail: FFWC said the Surma at Chhatak, Kushiyara at Markuli and Fenchuganj, and Someshwari at Kalmakanda were above danger level and the flood situation in Sylhet, Sunamganj, Netrokona, Sherpur and Mymensingh could deteriorate over two days.

title: 300+ Bangladeshis repatriated from SE Asia scam compounds
detail: The Expatriates' Welfare Ministry said more than 300 Bangladeshis rescued from cyber scam compounds in Cambodia, Laos, Vietnam and elsewhere have been repatriated; survivors reported paying recruiters up to about Tk 900,000.
attribution: Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment via Dhaka Tribune

title: BFIU to freeze 14,000 more gambling-linked MFS accounts
detail: A BFIU official said 10,000 MFS accounts were frozen the previous month and a further 14,000 would be frozen on an agency report; the Gambling Prevention Act 2026 took effect 1 July.

title: Load-shedding surges past 2,000 MW amid gas and coal shortfalls
detail: PGCB data showed the power shortage rising from 335 MW on 6 Aug to 2,167 MW on 8 Aug, driven by coal-handling problems and insufficient gas to power plants; Pabna reported 8-10 hour outages and Khulna 3-5 hours daily.
attribution: Power Grid Company of Bangladesh (PGCB) data via The Daily Star

title: Monsoon depression: ports keep signal No. 3
detail: The Met office told Chattogram, Cox's Bazar, Mongla and Payra ports to keep local cautionary signal No. 3 as a monsoon depression intensified over the southwest Bangladesh-West Bengal coast; fishing boats in the North Bay were told to stay near the coast.

title: Chinese/Taiwanese-run online fraud base found in Cox's Bazar resorts
detail: CID said a group of Chinese and Taiwanese nationals rented resorts and a residential building near Himchhari along Marine Drive and set up soundproofed rooms with thousands of iPhones and computers for international online fraud; six were remanded under the Cyber Security Act 2026 and four others are fugitives.

title: RSF: 481 killed in 513 road crashes in August
detail: Road Safety Foundation, compiling media reports, counted 513 road crashes in August 2026 killing 481 and injuring 664; motorcycles accounted for 176 deaths and pedestrians 102, with Bogura the deadliest district (37).

title: BGB seizes 1.4 million yaba tablets at Hnila
detail: BGB's 64 Battalion (Hnila border outpost) said a patrol acting on intelligence about smuggling from Myanmar arrested two suspects near the zero line with 1.4 million yaba tablets.

title: 63 foreigners held at scam hub in Chattogram building
detail: Police arrested 63 foreign nationals (Chinese, Pakistani, Laotian, Nepali, Vietnamese) running an online fraud operation from a seven-storey residential building in Chattogram, seizing 134 phones and 57 laptops.

title: Court freezes Tk 786 crore of Nagad-linked shares
detail: On an ACC petition, Dhaka Senior Special Judge Md Shahjahan Kabir froze Tk 786 crore in shares linked to former Nagad MD Tanvir Ahmed Mishuk and associates; ACC alleges about Tk 1,706 crore in government allowance funds was diverted and laundered abroad.

title: Dengue: 5 deaths, 1,484 admissions in 24 hours
detail: DGHS reported 5 dengue deaths (4 in Dhaka North City Corporation, 1 in Rangpur division) and 1,484 hospitalisations in the 24 hours to 08:00; year-to-date 58,400 cases and 176 deaths, with 4,132 patients in hospital.
attribution: Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) via The Daily Star

title: 480,000 yaba seized in Teknaf and Himchhari
detail: BGB's Ukhia battalion recovered 440,000 yaba tablets in two operations after carriers crossing from Myanmar dropped their loads, and DNC seized 40,000 from a tourist vehicle, arresting one man.
attribution: BGB and Department of Narcotics Control (DNC)

title: Dengue death toll for 2026 passes 200
detail: DGHS reported 6 dengue deaths and 1,868 admissions in 24 hours, bringing 2026 totals to 67,367 hospitalisations and 201 deaths; September's 104 deaths so far are the highest monthly toll of the year.
attribution: Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) via bdnews24

title: UNODC warns Bangladesh risks becoming scam hub
detail: A UNODC report released on 25 September warned that Bangladesh, Nepal and Sri Lanka risk becoming cybercrime hubs rather than just source countries of trafficking victims.

title: Bus rear-ends stationary bus on Dhaka-Bhanga Expressway
detail: Highway police said a bus struck another bus stopped for tyre repair at Bakhrerkandi, Shibchar, killing three on the spot and injuring at least 15.
attribution: Shibchar Highway Police via The Daily Star
